2	name: Auth Patterns
3	description: Production-grade authentication and authorization patterns across all stacks — the standard every Boldteq project must follow
4	type: reference
5	---
6	
7	## Core Principles (Stack-Agnostic)
8	
9	### 1. Identity Must Be Server-Validated
10	- Never trust client-side tokens or session data for authorization decisions
11	- Always revalidate the user's identity on the server for every protected operation
12	- Token validation happens at the middleware/gateway layer, not inside business logic
13	
14	### 2. Auth Is Day-One Infrastructure
15	- Auth is scaffolded before any feature code — never "added later"
16	- The auth system defines the data model (user → org → permissions → features)
17	- Every API route is protected by default; public routes are explicitly opted-in
18	
19	### 3. Session Architecture
20	- **Short-lived access tokens** (15 min) + **long-lived refresh tokens** (7-30 days)
21	- Refresh tokens stored HTTP-only, Secure, SameSite=Strict
22	- Access tokens never stored in localStorage — use memory or HTTP-only cookies
23	- Token rotation on every refresh — invalidate the old refresh token immediately
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Stack-Specific Patterns
28	
29	### Stack A — Supabase Auth (Next.js SaaS)
30	
31	**Server Components:**
32	```typescript
33	// Always use getUser(), never getSession() on server
34	const { data: { user }, error } = await supabase.auth.getUser()
35	if (!user) redirect('/login')
36	```
37	
38	**Middleware Protection:**
39	```typescript
40	// middleware.ts — broad route protection
41	const protectedPaths = ['/dashboard', '/settings', '/api/private']
42	if (protectedPaths.some(p => request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith(p))) {
43	  const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser()
44	  if (!user) return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', request.url))
45	}
46	```
47	
48	**RLS as Second Layer:**
49	- Supabase RLS policies enforce data access even if application logic has bugs
50	- Every table has `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` from creation
51	- Default deny — no policy means no access
52	- Standard pattern: `USING (auth.uid() = user_id)` for user-scoped data
53	- Org-scoped: `USING (org_id IN (SELECT org_id FROM org_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid()))`
54	
55	**OAuth Providers:**
56	- Google, GitHub, Twitter supported out of the box
57	- Always configure redirect URLs per environment (dev, preview, prod)
58	- Store provider tokens if API access needed (e.g., GitHub repos)
59	
60	### Stack B — Shopify App Auth (Remix)
61	
62	**Session Token Flow:**
63	```typescript
64	// Every loader/action starts with this — non-negotiable
65	const { admin, session } = await authenticate.admin(request)
66	// session.shop is the trusted identity — never from URL params
67	```
68	
69	**Storefront/Public Routes:**
70	- Validate Shopify origin via HMAC signature
71	- Use App Proxy for authenticated storefront requests
72	- Public API endpoints require origin validation or signed requests
73	
74	**Mandatory Webhooks:**
75	- `shop/redact` — GDPR shop data deletion
76	- `customers/redact` — GDPR customer data deletion
77	- `customers/data_request` — GDPR data export
78	- Must return 200 immediately, process asynchronously
79	
80	### Stack C — AI App Auth (Next.js + Supabase)
81	
82	- Same as Stack A foundation
83	- Additional: API key management for external AI service access
84	- Rate limiting per user tier (free: 10 req/min, pro: 100 req/min, enterprise: custom)
85	- Token usage tracking tied to user/org for billing
86	- Streaming endpoints still require auth — validate before opening SSE connection
87	
88	### Custom Stacks
89	
90	**NextAuth.js:**
91	- Configure providers in `[...nextauth].ts`
92	- Use `getServerSession()` for server-side auth checks
93	- Custom adapter for Prisma/Drizzle/Supabase
94	- JWT strategy for serverless, database strategy for traditional servers
95	
96	**Auth0 / Okta / Firebase:**
97	- Use official SDK middleware
98	- Validate JWT signature + claims on every API request
99	- Map external user ID to internal user record on first login
100	- Handle token refresh transparently in middleware
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Authorization Patterns
105	
106	### Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
107	```
108	Roles: owner > admin > member > viewer
109	Hierarchy: each role inherits all permissions of roles below it
110	```
111	
112	**Implementation:**
113	- Store role on `org_members` junction table, not on user
114	- Check permission in middleware or route handler, never in UI only
115	- UI hides elements, server enforces — both required
116	
117	### Feature Gating (Subscription-Based)
118	```
119	Free tier → basic features
120	Pro tier → advanced features + higher limits
121	Enterprise → custom features + unlimited
122	```
123	
124	**Implementation:**
125	- Check `subscription_status` + `plan_tier` server-side before executing feature
126	- Cache plan info on session/token to reduce DB lookups (invalidate on webhook)
127	- Feature flags for gradual rollout within tiers
128	
129	### Multi-Tenant Isolation
130	- Every query scoped to `org_id` — enforced at ORM/RLS level
131	- Cross-tenant data access is a P0 security incident
132	- Audit log every admin-level action with actor, target, timestamp
133	- Data export scoped to tenant — never leak cross-tenant data
134	
135	---
136	
137	## Security Checklist (Every Project)
138	
139	1. [ ] Passwords hashed with bcrypt (cost 12+) or Argon2
140	2. [ ] No secrets in client-side code or git history
141	3. [ ] CSRF protection on all state-changing operations
142	4. [ ] Rate limiting on auth endpoints (login: 5/min, signup: 3/min, reset: 2/min)
143	5. [ ] Account lockout after 10 failed attempts (30-min cooldown)
144	6. [ ] Secure password reset flow (time-limited token, single-use)
145	7. [ ] Session invalidation on password change
146	8. [ ] Email verification before granting full access
147	9. [ ] 2FA support for enterprise tier (TOTP preferred)
148	10. [ ] Audit log for sensitive operations (role changes, data export, deletion)
149	
150	---
151	
152	## Common Antipatterns (Never Do These)
153	
154	- Storing tokens in localStorage — XSS exposes them instantly
155	- Using URL query params for auth tokens — leaked in referrer headers and logs
156	- Trusting client-sent user IDs — always derive from server session
157	- Skipping rate limiting on auth endpoints — brute force will happen
158	- Shared service role keys across environments — isolate per env
159	- Rolling your own JWT library — use battle-tested libraries (jose, jsonwebtoken)
160	- Checking permissions only in the UI — server must enforce independently
161	
162	---
163

2	name: Quality Framework & Release Management
3	description: Definition of Done, acceptance criteria standards, release process, versioning, and hotfix protocol — the quality bar every Boldteq product must clear
4	type: reference
5	priority: high
6	---
7	
8	## 1. Definition of Done (DoD)
9	
10	A feature is DONE only when ALL of these are true:
11	
12	### Code Quality
13	- [ ] TypeScript strict mode — zero `any` types in production code
14	- [ ] All functions have explicit return types
15	- [ ] No ESLint warnings (errors are blocked at commit via husky)
16	- [ ] No `console.log` in production code (use structured logger)
17	- [ ] Code reviewed by Sage with PASS verdict
18	- [ ] No TODO comments without linked issue/ticket
19	
20	### Testing
21	- [ ] Unit tests for all business logic (≥ 80% coverage)
22	- [ ] Integration tests for API routes (happy path + error cases)
23	- [ ] E2E tests for critical user flows (auth, billing, main value prop)
24	- [ ] RLS tests for every database policy (Stack A/C)
25	- [ ] Accessibility tests pass (axe-core, no critical violations)
26	
27	### Functionality
28	- [ ] All acceptance criteria met and verified
29	- [ ] Error states handled (network error, validation error, server error)
30	- [ ] Loading states present (skeleton, spinner, or progress indicator)
31	- [ ] Empty states designed (first-time user, no data, search no results)
32	- [ ] Edge cases handled (long text, special characters, concurrent edits)
33	- [ ] Mobile responsive (if web) or adaptive layout (if desktop)
34	
35	### UI/UX
36	- [ ] Passes Sage's AI-Generated UI Detection Checklist (all 20 points)
37	- [ ] Follows `patterns/good/saas-brand-patterns.md` standards
38	- [ ] Follows `patterns/good/ui-ux-production-standards.md` rules
39	- [ ] shadcn/ui components composed into app-specific components (never raw)
40	- [ ] Consistent icon usage (Lucide React, strokeWidth 1.75, branded wrapper)
41	- [ ] Animations are purposeful (Framer Motion, not random CSS transitions)
42	- [ ] Typography hierarchy clear (one font, 4-5 sizes max)
43	- [ ] Color system consistent (semantic tokens, not hardcoded hex)
44	
45	### Security
46	- [ ] Auth enforced server-side on all protected routes
47	- [ ] Input validated with Zod on all API endpoints
48	- [ ] No secrets in client code or git history
49	- [ ] RLS policies active on all tables (Stack A/C)
50	- [ ] Rate limiting on public and auth endpoints
51	- [ ] CSRF protection on state-changing operations

54	- [ ] Every public page has unique title tag (50-60 chars, primary keyword first)
55	- [ ] Every public page has unique meta description (150-160 chars, with CTA)
56	- [ ] Exactly one H1 per page containing primary keyword

71	- [ ] Environment variables documented with descriptions
72	- [ ] Migration files have up and down migrations

75	
76	## 2. Acceptance Criteria Standards
77	
78	### How to Write Acceptance Criteria
79	Use the Given/When/Then format for behavioral criteria:
80	```
81	GIVEN a logged-in user on the Pro plan
82	WHEN they click "Export to CSV"
83	THEN a CSV file downloads containing all their filtered data
84	AND the file name includes the current date
85	AND a success toast appears for 3 seconds
86	```
87	
88	### Required Criteria for Every Feature
89	1. **Happy path** — the expected user flow works
90	2. **Error handling** — what happens when things go wrong
91	3. **Edge cases** — boundary conditions, empty states, limits
92	4. **Permissions** — who can and cannot access this
93	5. **Performance** — acceptable load time, response time
94	
95	### Anti-Criteria (Never Write These)
96	- "Should work correctly" — too vague, untestable
97	- "Nice UI" — define what "nice" means specifically
98	- "Fast" — define the metric (< 200ms API response, < 2s page load)
99	- "Handle errors" — specify which errors and how
100	
101	---
102	
103	## 3. Release Management
104	
105	### Versioning (Semantic Versioning)
106	```
107	MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
108	
109	MAJOR (1.0.0 → 2.0.0): Breaking changes, major redesign
110	MINOR (1.0.0 → 1.1.0): New features, backward compatible
111	PATCH (1.0.0 → 1.0.1): Bug fixes, performance improvements
112	```
113	
114	### Release Cadence
115	| Release Type | Frequency | Examples |
116	|-------------|-----------|---------|
117	| v1.0.0 (Initial) | End of build phase | First production deployment |
118	| Feature release | Per sprint (every 3 days) | New features, improvements |
119	| Patch release | As needed | Bug fixes, security patches |
120	| Hotfix | Immediate | P0 production issues |
121	
122	### Release Process
123	```
124	1. Feature branch → main (via PR)
125	2. Sage review PASS required
126	3. Luna tests all green
127	4. Zeph SEO audit PASS required (no P0/P1 SEO bugs on public pages)
128	5. Changelog updated (what changed, why)
129	6. Version bumped (semantic)
130	7. Bolt deploys to staging
131	8. Smoke test on staging (5-10 min manual or automated)
132	9. Bolt promotes to production
133	10. Hawk verifies health metrics
134	11. Mira logs release in project memory
135	```
136	
137	### Branch Strategy
138	```
139	main ← always deployable, protected
140	  └── feature/[slug] ← one branch per feature/story
141	  └── fix/[slug] ← one branch per bug fix
142	  └── hotfix/[slug] ← emergency fixes, branched from main
143	```
144	
145	- No develop branch — main is always deployable
146	- Feature branches are short-lived (max 2 days)
147	- Squash merge to main for clean history
148	- Branch protection: require PR review (Sage), passing tests (Luna)
149	
150	---
151	
152	## 4. Hotfix Protocol
153	
154	### When to Hotfix (vs. Normal Release)
155	- P0: Production down, data loss, security breach → HOTFIX IMMEDIATELY
156	- P1: Major feature broken, billing affected → HOTFIX WITHIN 4 HOURS
157	- P2: Minor feature broken, workaround exists → NEXT REGULAR RELEASE
158	- P3: Cosmetic, edge case → BACKLOG
159	
160	### Hotfix Process
161	```
162	1. Vex diagnoses root cause (max 30 min)
163	2. Vex implements fix on hotfix/[slug] branch
164	3. Luna runs targeted tests (affected area only)
165	4. Sage fast-track review (security + correctness only)
166	5. Bolt deploys directly to production
167	6. Hawk verifies fix is working
168	7. Mira logs incident + fix in project memory
169	8. Backfill: full test suite run, documentation updated
170	```
171	
172	### Rollback Protocol
173	If a hotfix makes things worse:
174	1. Bolt reverts to previous deployment (Vercel instant rollback)
175	2. Hawk confirms health restored
176	3. Vex gets more time for proper diagnosis
177	4. Never deploy the same broken fix twice
178	
179	---
180	
181	## 5. Code Review Standards (Sage)
182	
183	### Review Tiers
184	| Tier | Criteria | Verdict |
185	|------|----------|---------|
186	| PASS | No issues, ship it | Deploy approved |
187	| PASS WITH WARNINGS | Minor issues, non-blocking | Deploy approved, fix in next sprint |
188	| FAIL | Critical issues | Do not deploy, fix required |
189	
190	### What Gets FAIL
191	- Security vulnerability (exposed secrets, missing auth, SQL injection)
192	- Data integrity risk (missing validation, race condition, no transaction)
193	- Breaking change without migration
194	- Test coverage below 60% for new code
195	- P0 bug present in new code
196	- AI-generated UI detection score > 5/20 (too many AI tells)
197	
198	### What Gets PASS WITH WARNINGS
199	- Test coverage 60-80% (should be 80%+)
200	- Minor performance concern (N+1 query on low-traffic endpoint)
201	- Missing error handling on non-critical path
202	- Minor UI inconsistency (spacing off by a few pixels)
203	- Missing loading state on non-critical feature
204	
205	---
206	
207	## 6. Performance Standards
208	
209	### Web Vitals (Non-Negotiable)
210	| Metric | Target | Measured By |
211	|--------|--------|-------------|
212	| LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) | < 2.5s | Lighthouse, Vercel Analytics |
213	| FID (First Input Delay) | < 100ms | Lighthouse |
214	| CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) | < 0.1 | Lighthouse |
215	| TTFB (Time to First Byte) | < 600ms | Vercel Analytics |
216	| Bundle size (initial JS) | < 200KB gzipped | Build analysis |
217	
218	### API Performance
219	| Metric | Target |
220	|--------|--------|

222	| API response (p95) | < 1s |

227	### Performance Review Process
228	1. Lighthouse audit on every PR (automated in CI)
229	2. Bundle size check (fail if increased by > 10KB without justification)
230	3. API response time check (fail if p95 > 1s on critical endpoints)
231	4. Monthly performance review by Hawk (trending analysis)

235	## 7. Dependency Management
236	
237	### Update Policy
238	| Dependency Type | Update Frequency | Process |
239	|----------------|-----------------|---------|
240	| Security patches | Immediately | Automated via Dependabot/Renovate |
241	| Minor versions | Weekly batch | Review changelog, run tests |
242	| Major versions | Quarterly review | Spike: evaluate breaking changes, plan migration |
243	| Framework (Next.js, Remix) | Per major release | Evaluate within 2 weeks, migrate within 1 month |
244	
245	### Dependency Rules
246	- No dependency without justification (every npm package is an attack surface)
247	- Prefer well-maintained packages (> 1000 GitHub stars, recent commits)
248	- Lock files (`package-lock.json`) always committed
249	- Audit output clean: `npm audit` must show 0 critical/high vulnerabilities
250	- If a package hasn't been updated in 12+ months, find an alternative

256	| Severity | Impact | Response Time | Resolution Time |
257	|----------|--------|---------------|-----------------|
258	| P0 — Critical | Production down, data loss, security breach | Immediate | < 1 hour |
259	| P1 — High | Major feature broken, billing impacted | < 1 hour | < 4 hours |
260	| P2 — Medium | Feature degraded, workaround available | < 4 hours | Next sprint |
261	| P3 — Low | Cosmetic issue, edge case | Next business day | Backlog |

270	## 9. Technical Debt Management
271	
272	### Debt Categories
273	| Category | Example | Priority |
274	|----------|---------|----------|
275	| Security debt | Missing rate limiting, outdated deps | Fix immediately |
276	| Performance debt | N+1 queries, missing indexes | Fix within 1 sprint |
277	| Code quality debt | Duplicated logic, missing types | Fix when touching the file |
278	| Test debt | Missing tests for critical paths | Fix before adding features |
279	| Architecture debt | Tight coupling, missing abstraction | Plan migration, execute in dedicated sprint |

282	- 20% of each sprint allocated to debt reduction
283	- Security and performance debt are non-negotiable — fix immediately
284	- Code quality debt fixed opportunistically (boy scout rule: leave code better than you found it)
285	- Architecture debt requires a spike first, then a planned sprint

46	## SEO Architecture Patterns

48	### URL Strategy for SaaS
49	```
50	/ → Homepage (brand + primary keyword)
51	/features → Feature overview (secondary keywords)
52	/features/[feature] → Individual feature (long-tail keywords)
53	/pricing → Pricing page (transactional intent)

59	/templates or /examples → User resources (massive long-tail surface)
60	/compare/[competitor] → Comparison pages (bottom-funnel commercial intent)
61	```

63	### Internal Linking Rules
64	1. Every page links to 3-5 related internal pages
65	2. Footer links to all major sections (pricing, features, blog, docs)
66	3. Blog posts link to feature pages (informational → commercial)
67	4. Feature pages link to pricing (commercial → transactional)
68	5. No orphan pages — every page reachable within 3 clicks from homepage
69	6. Use descriptive anchor text (not "click here" or "learn more")
70	
71	### Content Clusters (Hub & Spoke Model)
72	```
73	Hub Page: /features/analytics (pillar content, 2000+ words)
74	├── Spoke: /blog/how-to-track-user-engagement
75	├── Spoke: /blog/analytics-dashboard-best-practices
76	├── Spoke: /blog/what-metrics-matter-for-saas
77	├── Spoke: /docs/analytics-api-reference
78	└── Spoke: /templates/analytics-dashboard-template

80	All spokes link back to hub. Hub links to all spokes.
81	This builds topical authority for "analytics" keyword cluster.

144	## SEO Antipatterns (Never Do These)
145	
146	- **Client-side only rendering** — Google may not execute JS, content invisible
147	- **Same title tag on every page** — Google sees these as duplicates
148	- **Keyword stuffing** — unnatural repetition gets penalized
149	- **Hidden text or links** — Google penalizes cloaking
150	- **Thin doorway pages** — low-quality pages targeting many keywords
151	- **Ignoring Search Console errors** — crawl errors compound over time
152	- **No canonical URLs** — duplicate content dilutes rankings
153	- **Blocking CSS/JS in robots.txt** — Google needs to render the page
154	- **Changing URLs without redirects** — lose all accumulated ranking authority
155	- **Publishing AI-generated content without editing** — Google's Helpful Content Update devalues it

3	## Navigation Patterns
4	
5	### Sidebar Navigation (Linear Model)
6	- **Collapsible sidebar**: 240px expanded, collapses to 60px icons only
7	- **Keyboard shortcuts**: Cmd+B (toggle sidebar), Cmd+J (quick open), Cmd+K (search)
8	- **Icon + label layout**: Icons always visible, labels hide when collapsed
9	- **Active state**: Left border accent (3-4px), never just highlight background
10	- **Secondary nav**: Nested items indented 12px with subtle hierarchy
11	- **Pinned items**: Let users customize what shows in sidebar (Linear pins projects)
12	- **Search within nav**: Cmd+Shift+P shows filtered command palette
13	
14	**Pattern**: Collapsibility = power user feature + mobile solution. Icons must be 100% clear without labels.
15	
16	### Workspace Switching (Notion Model)
17	- **Switcher at top**: Shows current workspace + icon, dropdown reveals all workspaces
18	- **Recent workspaces**: Pin 3-4 favorites, rest accessible via "See all"
19	- **Quick switch keyboard**: Cmd+Shift+P or similar for workspace switcher
20	- **Profile menu**: Separate from workspace switcher, always in top-right
21	
22	**Pattern**: Workspace = different context, not just different team. Switching should feel instant and safe.
23	
24	### Hierarchical Navigation (Linear Model)
25	- **Breadcrumb trail**: Home > Category > Subcategory, updates as you navigate
26	- **Sidebar categories**: Main sections with count badges (e.g., "Events (23)")
27	- **Sticky subheader**: Category title + filters stay visible as user scrolls
28	- **Icon + text nav**: Icons left, labels right, both required for comprehension
29	- **Mobile breadcrumb**: Tap to go back, not hamburger menu
30	
31	**Pattern**: Breadcrumbs prevent "where am I?" anxiety. Sidebar shows current location emphasis.

35	## Dashboard Patterns

38	- **Cards, not dashboards**: Each project as horizontal card, status on right
39	- **No pie charts**: Use progress bars instead (circular charts waste space)
40	- **Stat hierarchy**: Primary metric (large, bold) + secondary metrics (small, muted)
41	- **Status color coding**: Green/yellow/red for on-time/at-risk/overdue (semantic colors only)
42	- **Avoid**: Traffic lights, gauges, needles, 3D effects

45	```
46	[Project Icon] Project Name
47	Created • Updated • Members (3)                    On Track  [████████░░]
48	```

50	### Deployment Status (Vercel Model)
51	- **Timeline view**: Most recent at top, chronological, minimal styling
52	- **Status badge**: Compact color pill (8px border-radius) + status text
53	- **Metadata in gray**: Time, duration, triggered by, branch
54	- **Log streaming**: Real-time updates without spinner (skeleton -> live content)
55	- **No loading spinners**: Skeleton placeholder or progress indicator instead

57	**Pattern**: Minimal = fast perception. Use color + text, not icons + animation.

60	- **Clean line chart**: No grid, no axis labels (only hover tooltip)
61	- **Summary cards above chart**: Current value (largest), previous period, % change (muted)
62	- **Contextual filter**: Date range selector, always visible
63	- **Export button**: CSV/JSON accessible but not prominent

211	## Product Thinking (Anti-Overengineering)
212	
213	Before building ANY feature, every agent must ask:
214	1. **What is the real user goal?** — Not what they asked for, what they're trying to ACHIEVE
215	2. **What is the simplest way to achieve it?** — Fewer clicks, fewer screens, fewer steps
216	3. **Is this feature overcomplicated?** — Would Stripe, Linear, or Notion build it this way?
217	4. **Am I building for edge cases that don't exist yet?** — Solve the 95% case first
218	
219	Optimize for: **Simplicity → Clarity → Speed to value → Conversion**
220	
221	The enemy is overengineering. If a feature needs a tutorial to explain, it's too complex. If a setting has 10 options when 3 would cover 95% of users, simplify it.
222	
223	---
224	
225	## Real-World Reliability
226	
227	Every agent must consider real-world conditions, not just happy-path:
228	- **Invalid inputs** — empty strings, SQL injection, XSS, massive payloads, Unicode edge cases
229	- **Large data** — what happens with 10K rows? 100K? Does the table paginate? Does the query timeout?
230	- **Slow APIs** — what if the AI endpoint takes 30 seconds? Is there a loading state? A timeout? A retry?
231	- **Network delays** — what if the user is on 3G? Does the UI feel broken or gracefully degrade?
232	- **Unexpected user actions** — double-click submit, back button, refresh mid-operation, tab away and come back
233	- **Concurrent access** — two users editing the same resource, race conditions on credit deduction
234	
235	The system must remain **stable and predictable** under all conditions. If it can't handle a condition gracefully, it must fail with a clear error message and recovery action.
236	
237	---
238	
239	## System Consistency
240	
241	When adding anything new to an existing project:
242	1. **Reuse existing components** — check what's already built before creating new ones
243	2. **Match existing patterns** — if the project uses React Query for data, don't add raw useEffect
244	3. **Avoid duplication** — if a utility exists in `lib/`, use it. Don't create a second one.
245	4. **Ensure clean integration** — new features must fit the existing architecture, not sit alongside it
246	5. **Never build in isolation** — every new component must work with the existing nav, layout, auth, and state management
247	
248	If adding a feature would require breaking existing patterns → that's a refactor task, not a feature task. Flag it.
249	
250	---
251	
252	## Security as Global Principle
253	
254	Security is NOT just Koda's job. Every agent must think about security:
255	- **Nova**: research competitor security incidents and data handling
256	- **Arya**: design auth, RLS, and data isolation from day one
257	- **Riko**: scaffold with security defaults (HTTPS, CORS, CSP headers)
258	- **Vega**: never put sensitive data in URLs, visible form fields, or screenshots
259	- **Koda**: input validation, parameterized queries, auth checks on every endpoint
260	- **Quill**: never include customer data in copy examples
261	- **Luna**: test auth boundaries, permission escalation, data leakage
262	- **Sage**: full security audit (the main gate, but not the only one)
263	- **Bolt**: secrets in env vars only, no credentials in build artifacts
264	- **Hawk**: monitor for unauthorized access patterns, unusual API usage
265	
266	If ANY agent spots a security risk → flag immediately, don't wait for Sage's review.
267	
268	---
269	
270	## Deployment Readiness (Global)
271	
272	Every agent's output must be deployable — not just "works on my machine":
273	- **No local-only assumptions** — no hardcoded `localhost`, no absolute file paths, no local-only file references
274	- **Environment variables handled** — every secret, URL, and config value comes from env vars
275	- **Dependencies correctly defined** — every import has a corresponding package.json entry with pinned version
276	- **Build passes** — `npm run build` succeeds with zero warnings before declaring anything done
277	- **No dev-only code in production** — no `console.log` spam, no debug panels, no test data
278	
279	---
280	
281	## Error Recovery Protocol
282	
283	When an approach FAILS (build error, wrong pattern, impossible constraint):
284	
285	```
286	1. STOP — Don't keep pushing a broken approach
287	2. DIAGNOSE — What specifically failed and why?
288	3. EVALUATE — Is this a fixable issue or a wrong approach?
289	   ├── Fixable → Fix the specific issue, verify, continue
290	   └── Wrong approach → Go to step 4
291	4. SIMPLIFY — Can the requirement be met with a simpler approach?
292	   ├── Yes → Rebuild with simpler approach
293	   └── No → Go to step 5
294	5. REBUILD — Start fresh with a different architecture
295	   - Don't carry broken assumptions forward
296	   - Document what failed and why for Mira
297	6. ESCALATE — If 3 attempts fail → flag to Rex with full context
298	   - What was tried
299	   - What failed
300	   - What the blocker is
301	```
302	
303	**Never stay stuck in a broken solution.** Sunk cost doesn't apply to code — if the approach is wrong, throw it away and start clean.
304	
305	---
306	
307	## Quality Bar — The "Ship It" Test
308	
309	Before ANY agent declares work complete, answer these questions:
310	
311	```
312	Would I be comfortable if Yash demo'd this to a paying customer RIGHT NOW?
313	├── YES → Ship it
314	└── NO → What's missing?
315	    ├── "The design looks basic" → Improve it (Vega/Koda)
316	    ├── "Some edge cases aren't handled" → Handle them (Koda)
317	    ├── "Tests are incomplete" → Write them (Luna)
318	    ├── "Security hasn't been reviewed" → Review it (Sage)
319	    ├── "Copy is generic" → Rewrite it (Quill)
320	    ├── "Performance is unknown" → Measure it (Zeph/Sage)
321	    └── "It works but feels fragile" → Harden it (Koda/Vex)
322	```
323	
324	If the answer to ANY of these is "no" → the work is NOT done. Fix it.
325	
326	---
327	
328	## The Standard We Compare Against
329	
330	Every output must match or exceed the quality of these real products:
331	
332	| Category | Benchmark | What to match |
333	|----------|-----------|---------------|
334	| **Dashboard UX** | Linear, Vercel | Clean, fast, keyboard-first, instant feedback |
335	| **Data tables** | Stripe Dashboard | Sortable, filterable, exportable, responsive |
336	| **Forms** | Notion | Inline validation, auto-save, smooth transitions |
337	| **Settings** | GitHub Settings | Grouped sections, danger zone, clear save feedback |
338	| **Auth flows** | Clerk, Supabase Auth | Social login, magic link, password strength, smooth redirect |
339	| **Admin panels** | Shopify Admin | Polaris patterns, resource management, bulk actions |
340	| **Error states** | Linear | Friendly message, retry action, help link |
341	| **Loading states** | Vercel | Skeleton matching final layout, no spinners, no blank pages |
342	| **Mobile** | Any top SaaS | Touch-first, no horizontal scroll, drawer navigation |
343	
344	If our output wouldn't look at home next to these → it's not done.
345	
346	---
347	
348	## Decision Framework
349	
350	When multiple approaches exist, choose based on this priority:
351	
352	```
353	1. Correctness — does it work for ALL cases? (not just happy path)
354	2. User Experience — is it intuitive, fast, and delightful?
355	3. Scalability — will it work with 10x data/users?
356	4. Maintainability — can another agent understand and modify it?
357	5. Performance — is it fast enough? (LCP < 2.5s, no jank)
358	6. Simplicity — is it as simple as it can be WITHOUT sacrificing 1-5?
359	```
360	
361	Simplicity is LAST, not first. We never choose the easy way if it compromises the user experience or correctness.
362

1	---
2	name: AI App Stack Knowledge (Stack C)
3	description: Accumulated patterns for building AI-powered products with Next.js, Supabase, and Vercel AI SDK
4	type: reference
5	stack: ai-nextjs-supabase
6	---
7	
8	## Stack
9	Next.js 14+ (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui + Supabase + Vercel AI SDK + Anthropic/OpenAI SDK + Dodo Payments + Vercel
10	
11	## Projects Built On This Stack
12	*(None shipped yet — patterns derived from industry standards and Vercel AI SDK docs)*
13	
14	## Critical Patterns
15	
16	### AI SDK Integration
17	- Use `@ai-sdk/anthropic` or `@ai-sdk/openai` as the provider
18	- `streamText()` for streaming chat responses — always stream, never block
19	- `generateText()` only for background/batch operations (not user-facing)
20	- `generateObject()` with Zod schema for structured output extraction
21	- Always set `maxTokens` to prevent runaway costs
22	
23	### Streaming Architecture
24	```typescript
25	// app/api/chat/route.ts
26	import { streamText } from 'ai'
27	import { anthropic } from '@ai-sdk/anthropic'
28	
29	export async function POST(req: Request) {
30	  const { messages } = await req.json()
31	
32	  const result = streamText({
33	    model: anthropic('claude-sonnet-4-5-20250514'),
34	    messages,
35	    maxTokens: 4096,
36	    system: 'System prompt here...',
37	  })
38	
39	  return result.toDataStreamResponse()
40	}
41	```
42	
43	```typescript
44	// Client-side with useChat
45	'use client'
46	import { useChat } from 'ai/react'
47	
48	export function Chat() {
49	  const { messages, input, handleInputChange, handleSubmit, isLoading } = useChat()
50	  // Render messages with streaming indicator
51	}
52	```
53	
54	### Rate Limiting (Critical for AI Apps)
55	```typescript
56	// Upstash Redis rate limiter
57	import { Ratelimit } from '@upstash/ratelimit'
58	import { Redis } from '@upstash/redis'
59	
60	const ratelimit = new Ratelimit({
61	  redis: Redis.fromEnv(),
62	  limiter: Ratelimit.slidingWindow(10, '1 m'), // 10 req/min
63	  analytics: true,
64	})
65	
66	// In API route — check before calling AI
67	const { success, limit, remaining } = await ratelimit.limit(userId)
68	if (!success) {
69	  return new Response('Rate limit exceeded', { status: 429 })
70	}
71	```
72	
73	### Token Usage Tracking
74	```sql
75	-- ai_usage table
76	id, user_id, org_id, model, input_tokens, output_tokens,
77	total_tokens, cost_usd, endpoint, created_at
78	
79	-- Aggregate per billing period for metered billing
80	SELECT user_id, SUM(total_tokens) as period_tokens, SUM(cost_usd) as period_cost
81	FROM ai_usage
82	WHERE created_at BETWEEN billing_period_start AND billing_period_end
83	GROUP BY user_id
84	```
85	
86	### Prompt Management
87	- Store system prompts in database or config — not hardcoded in route handlers
88	- Version prompts: track which prompt version produced which output
89	- A/B test prompts by tracking output quality metrics per version
90	- Never expose system prompts to the client
91	
92	### Tool Use / Function Calling
93	```typescript
94	const result = streamText({
95	  model: anthropic('claude-sonnet-4-5-20250514'),
96	  messages,
97	  tools: {
98	    searchDatabase: {
99	      description: 'Search the product database',
100	      parameters: z.object({
101	        query: z.string(),
102	        category: z.enum(['electronics', 'clothing', 'food']),
103	      }),
104	      execute: async ({ query, category }) => {
105	        return await db.products.search(query, category)
106	      },
107	    },
108	  },
109	  maxSteps: 5, // Allow multi-step tool use
110	})
111	```
112	
113	### Error Handling for AI
114	```typescript
115	try {
116	  const result = await streamText({ ... })
117	  return result.toDataStreamResponse()
118	} catch (error) {
119	  if (error.status === 429) {
120	    // Provider rate limit — queue and retry with exponential backoff
121	    return new Response('AI service busy, please retry', { status: 503 })
122	  }
123	  if (error.status === 400) {
124	    // Bad request — likely prompt too long, truncate context
125	    return new Response('Request too large', { status: 400 })
126	  }
127	  // Log to monitoring, return generic error
128	  console.error('AI error:', error)
129	  return new Response('AI service unavailable', { status: 500 })
130	}
131	```
132	
133	## AI UX Patterns
134	
135	### Chat Interface
136	- Streaming text appears character-by-character (not chunk-by-chunk)
137	- Typing indicator while model processes (before first token)
138	- Stop generation button during streaming
139	- Copy/regenerate buttons on each response
140	- Message history with search
141	- Conversation threads/branching for power users
142	
143	### Non-Chat AI Features
144	- Processing indicator with estimated time for batch operations
145	- Inline suggestions (like Notion AI) — appear contextually, not in a chat
146	- AI-generated content clearly labeled but not in an annoying way
147	- Edit/refine flow: generate → review → modify → accept
148	- Undo AI actions easily
149	
150	### Loading States for AI
151	- Skeleton + "Thinking..." for <3 seconds
152	- Progress steps for longer operations ("Analyzing... Generating... Refining...")
153	- Estimated time remaining for batch operations
154	- Cancel button always available
155	
156	## Cost Management
157	
158	### Per-Request Cost Tracking
159	- Log every AI API call with model, tokens, and calculated cost
160	- Dashboard showing daily/weekly/monthly AI spend
161	- Alerts at 50%, 80%, 100% of budget thresholds
162	- Auto-disable non-critical AI features if budget exceeded
163	
164	### Model Selection Strategy
165	```
166	User-facing chat → Claude Sonnet (balanced quality/speed/cost)
167	Background processing → Claude Haiku (fast, cheap)
168	Complex reasoning → Claude Opus (best quality, higher cost)
169	Simple classification → Claude Haiku
170	Embeddings → text-embedding-3-small (OpenAI)
171	```
172	
173	### Caching Strategy
174	- Cache identical prompts + identical context → same response (TTL 1 hour)
175	- Semantic cache for similar queries (embedding similarity > 0.95)
176	- Cache structured outputs aggressively (classification, extraction)
177	- Never cache personalized responses
178	
179	## Common Gotchas
180	- Vercel serverless function timeout: 10s on Hobby, 60s on Pro — long AI calls need streaming or background jobs
181	- Edge functions can't use Node.js-specific APIs — use Edge-compatible AI SDK
182	- Supabase RLS still applies — AI-generated queries must respect user's data scope
183	- Token limits: always count tokens before sending (use `tiktoken` or provider's tokenizer)
184	- Prompt injection: validate and sanitize user input before including in prompts
185	- Model versioning: pin model versions in production, test new versions in staging
186	
187	## Deployment (Vercel)
188	- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` — never `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefixed
189	- `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` + `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` for rate limiting
190	- Use Vercel Edge Functions for streaming responses (lower latency)
191	- Set function `maxDuration` in route config for long-running AI calls
192	- Monitor Vercel function invocations — AI routes will be your highest volume
193

2	name: Pinzo — Shopify ZIP Code Delivery Checker
3	description: Project-specific decisions, patterns, and lessons for Pinzo
4	type: project
5	stack: B (React Router 7 + Polaris v13 + Prisma)
6	status: active
7	created: 2026-04-03
8	---
9	
10	## Project Overview
11	
12	**What:** Shopify embedded app that lets merchants configure ZIP code-based delivery rules. Storefront widget lets customers check delivery availability by entering their ZIP code.
13	
14	**Stack:** React Router 7 + @shopify/polaris v13 + Prisma v6 + SQLite (dev) / PostgreSQL (prod) + Vite v6
15	
16	**Deploy:** Railway (single instance)
17	
18	**Key Models:** Session, ZipCode, DeliveryRule, WaitlistEntry, WidgetConfig, Subscription, FeatureRequest, FeatureVote
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Architecture Decisions
23	
24	### GDPR Webhooks: Partner Dashboard, Not TOML
25	**Date:** 2026-04-03
26	**Decision:** GDPR webhook topics (`customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact`) are configured in Shopify Partner Dashboard > App Setup > Privacy, NOT in `shopify.app.toml`.
27	**Why:** Adding these topics to TOML causes `shopify app deploy` to fail with "The following topic is invalid". Route handler files still exist in `app/routes/`, but registration is external.
28	**Impact:** Global — applies to ALL Shopify apps, not just Pinzo. Updated in `stacks/shopify/core/shopify-app.md` and `stacks/shopify/build/webhooks.md`.
29	
30	### Rate Limiting: In-Memory for Single-Instance Deploy
31	**Date:** 2026-04-03
32	**Decision:** Built in-memory rate limiter (`app/utils/rate-limit.server.ts`) using sliding window counters per key.
33	**Why:** Railway runs a single instance. No Redis dependency needed. Clean cleanup loop prevents memory leaks.
34	**Limits:** zip-check: 60 req/min, widget-config: 30 req/min, waitlist: 10 req/min.
35	**Upgrade path:** If scaling to multiple instances, replace with Upstash Redis rate limiter (same interface, distributed store).
36	**Usage Metric:** 0
37	**Knowledge Version:** v1
38	
39	### Widget UI: Visual Grouping Over Flat Stacking
40	**Date:** 2026-04-03
41	**Decision:** Redesigned widget result card from flat vertical stack to 4 grouped sections with dividers.
42	**Why:** All info (message, ETA, delivery date, timeline, schedule, badges) stacked vertically with uniform styling created a wall of text. Visual grouping makes the widget scannable.
43	**Groups:** (1) Primary Info (message + ETA + delivery date), (2) Timeline (ORDER -> SHIPS -> DELIVER), (3) Scheduling (days + cutoff + countdown), (4) Badges (COD + Free Delivery as pill row).
44	**Rule:** Dividers only render when adjacent groups have content (no empty dividers).
45	**Usage Metric:** 0
46	**Knowledge Version:** v1
47	
48	### Admin Widget Preview Must Mirror Storefront Exactly
49	**Date:** 2026-04-03
50	**Decision:** Admin widget preview (React/Polaris) and storefront widget (Liquid + vanilla JS) must use identical CSS class names, conditional rendering logic, and section structure.
51	**Why:** Merchants configure the widget in admin and expect what they see in the preview to match the storefront exactly. Any divergence causes confusion and support tickets.
52	**Enforcement:** When changing the Liquid template, always update the React preview in `app.widget.tsx` in the same commit, and vice versa.
53	**Usage Metric:** 0
54	**Knowledge Version:** v1
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Compliance Audit Findings (2026-04-03)
59	
60	### GDPR Data Cleanup Gap
61	**Finding:** `FeatureRequest` and `FeatureVote` models were NOT being deleted in `app/uninstalled` and `shop/redact` webhook handlers.
62	**Fix:** Added deletion of both models to both handlers.
63	**Rule:** Every new Prisma model with a `shop` field MUST be added to both `webhooks.app.uninstalled.tsx` and `webhooks.shop.redact.tsx`.
64	
65	### Database Index Performance
66	**Finding:** `Session`, `ZipCode`, and `FeatureRequest` models lacked `@@index([shop])`, causing slow queries as data grows.
67	**Fix:** Added `@@index([shop])` to all models queried by shop.
68	**Rule:** Every model with a `shop` field MUST have `@@index([shop])` in the Prisma schema.
69	
70	### Hardcoded Secrets in Source
71	**Finding:** Admin shop domain and Chatwoot token were hardcoded in source files.
72	**Fix:** Moved to environment variables (`ADMIN_SHOP`, `CHATWOOT_WEBSITE_TOKEN`). Created `.env.example`.
73	**Rule:** Never hardcode any value that changes between environments.
74	
75	### CSS Sanitization Gap
76	**Finding:** Widget custom CSS was sanitized in the public API response but NOT in the admin preview.
77	**Fix:** Added identical CSS sanitization to admin widget preview.
78	**Rule:** Sanitize user-provided CSS at every render point, not just one.
79
